decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with vertical through contacts build directly on the firm's core drilling, polishing and bonding know-how, so it can interpret results and refine the product through its own R&D.
Carrier wafers for small-diameter handling extend the firm's established carrier and thin-wafer handling offer and fit its strategic push toward reusable carriers.

The Cu-interposer glass wafer leverages existing glass structuring and through-via expertise and matches the advanced-packaging trend, which justifies continued development despite metallization being a newer skill.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand reuses the existing standard glass and quartz wafer portfolio at low marginal cost and broadens market reach without new knowledge requirements.

Glass-based circuit boards sit far from the firm's wafer-level knowledge base and its PCB-type customers, so the firm has limited absorptive capacity to learn from early results, and the resources fit better with its core substrate business.
